newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 28.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's Daily Variety:
* News Corp unit 20th Century Fox's "Volcano" posted $14.7 million in ticket sales this weekend, 20 percent less than the opening of Universal's "Dante's Peak".
* Universal's acquisition of specialty outlet October Films will be completed shortly and formally announced at the Cannes Film Festival, sources close to the deal confirmed.
* General Electric NBC's Thursday powerhouse lineup got off to a strong sweeps start, but Westinghouse's CBS showed strength on Friday and Saturday.
* Construction company Bouygues, has retained French bank Societe Generale and its U.S. investment banking partner Bannon & Co to find a buyer for its film production house Ciby 2000, sources say.

* Time Warner vice chairman Ted Turner is personally and energetically urging networks to reject News Corp Chairman Rupert Murdoch's ASkyB DBS service set for launch this fall, say industry lobbyists involved in negotiations between the networks and News Corp.
* From the looks of the projects in development for 1998, it seems clear that syndicators have not given up the idea that game shows could stage a comeback.
* William James Edwards Jr, the guiding force behind Newport Beach-based Edwards Cinemas, died on Saturday, apparently of a heart attack, at the age of 90.
